Definition: from G303 and G2775 (in its original sense); to sum up:--briefly comprehend, gather together in one.
BiblicalUsage: The word means to sum up, to gather together under one head: every commandment — thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not covet — is briefly comprehended in this saying, 'Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself'; and in the fullness of times God will gather together in one all things in Christ, both in heaven and on earth. One verse sums up the law in love, and the other sums up the whole creation in Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for summing up carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the two gatherings — the whole law gathered into loving your neighbour, and all things gathered into Christ.
